basis: Attention metric definitions for ScaleSerum Vision Lab. The six metrics and their descriptions come from the Vision Lab prototype approved by management. Everything expressed as a number here is either a documented measurement rule or null - nothing is invented.
unconfirmed_business_values: whether psychological triggers affect the overall score
how_to_configure: Every business value below is null on purpose. null means 'management has not decided'. Fill a value in, bump framework_version, redeploy - no Python changes are needed. scoring.py reports which of these were still null for every analysis it produces, so a placeholder can never be mistaken for a decision.
rating_scale_note: Maps each rating level to a fraction of score_max, for the one metric (clarity) that blends an LLM rating with measurements. null means no business mapping exists, so scoring.py spaces the levels uniformly over [0,1] and reports rating_scale_mode='uniform_placeholder'.

metrics.name: Attention
metrics.label: captures initial gaze
metrics.note: Measured over the first hook_seconds only. No LLM input.

metrics.name: Focus
metrics.label: attention on the key message
metrics.note: The key message region is named by the LLM and matched by Python to a detected box. A frame with no match is EXCLUDED from the denominator, never scored zero.

metrics.name: Cognitive Demand
metrics.label: effort to understand - lower is better
metrics.note: Entirely measured. No LLM input. Inverted before it enters the overall score.

metrics.name: Clarity
metrics.label: message + CTA are unambiguous
metrics.llm_rating_weight_note: How much of this score comes from the LLM's ordinal rating versus the measured CTA signals. null means an equal split, reported as a placeholder.
metrics.note: The only metric an LLM contributes to, and it contributes a RATING, never a number.

metrics.name: Brand Memory
metrics.label: likelihood brand is remembered
metrics.note: peak_overlap - whether the brand is on screen during top-quartile attention moments - is the signal that distinguishes a logo that is seen from a logo that is merely present.

metrics.name: Engagement
metrics.label: pull to keep watching
metrics.note: Derived from the shape of the attention timeline, which is itself a composite index - see timeline below.

weights.note: A null weight on a metric means equal weighting. Set a positive number per metric to override, and flip metric_weights_confirmed so the API stops reporting the weighting as a placeholder.

bands_note: Score bands / pass-fail thresholds for the overall score. null means none are configured, and the API returns band=null with band_reason='thresholds_not_configured'. Do NOT copy Script Lab's 90/70/50 ad-script bands here - they carry no authority over creative attention.

timeline.basis_note: A saliency map sums to 1 on every frame, so it cannot say whether a frame held the viewer. This index is a composite over the terms below. It is NOT measured attention and must never be presented as such.

index_terms.note: share of saliency mass in the top 5% of pixels
mean absolute luma difference from the previous frame
maximum saliency mass on a detected face box
1 - earth mover's distance between consecutive maps
negative term: words / (reading_speed x shot seconds)
recency of the last shot change

engagement_line.note: The same function with novelty and motion up-weighted and concentration down-weighted. One function, two coefficient sets, so the two lines cannot drift apart in meaning.

timeline.hook_seconds_note: How much of the opening counts as the hook, for the Attention metric and the Halo Effect trigger. 3.0 s is the platform convention for a counted video view; confirm or replace.
timeline.weak_zone_note: A weak zone is attention below weak_threshold for at least min_weak_seconds. Both are business decisions about what counts as a dead zone; the placeholders are used until they are set, and every response says so.

reading_speed_note: Average adult reading speed in a non-reading context, used to compute whether on-screen copy can actually be read in the time it is held. 4 w/s is the figure the Vision Lab prototype cites and reports to the user. Confirm or replace - it is quoted verbatim in fix recommendations.

sampling.min_duration_note: Below this a video is not scored. null means no minimum is configured, so every video is analysed.

calibration.note: Raw saliency statistics have no natural 0-100 meaning. Until the analysed corpus reaches min_n creatives, scores use documented absolute anchors and report calibration='provisional_absolute'. A score must never imply a percentile while the reference set is small.

saliency_model.name: UNISAL
saliency_model.note: Set by the Phase 2 bake-off. licence is recorded here because several published saliency checkpoints are research-only and this is a commercial product. sha256 is verified at worker boot - a silently swapped model would change every score invisibly.
saliency_model.licence_note: The weights ship inside the Apache-2.0 repository. Training data included Hollywood-2 and UCF-Sports - see vision_lab/BAKEOFF_LICENCES.md before any client-facing use.
saliency_model.citation: Droste, Chen & Noble, Unified Image and Video Saliency Modelling, ECCV 2020
